examples.name: Default
examples.summary: All four rules plus the corner registration squares. Toggle `hatch`, `marks` and `borders` to see the frame change.

examples.name: Borders
examples.summary: Every `borders` value side by side. `y` is the full-bleed band that keeps only the two dividing rules; `none` hands every edge over to a surrounding grid and contributes just the corner marks.

examples.name: Marks
examples.summary: Each pair of corner ticks is drawn independently. `top` and `bottom` are what a stack needs: the frame above keeps its `bottom` pair and the frame below asks for `bottom` only, so a shared junction carries one mark per corner instead of two a few pixels apart.

examples.name: Hatch
examples.summary: The vertical hatch-line texture, faded toward the edges and rendered behind the content.

examples.name: Flush
examples.summary: `flush` names the sides a neighbour already draws, so it works on both axes. Vertically, the lower frame is `flush` (shorthand for `top`) with `marks="bottom"`; horizontally, the right-hand frame is `flush="left"` with `marks="right"`. Either way the shared edge reads as one hairline with one mark per corner, instead of two rules and four ticks. It is a subtraction from the frame's own side set, not an offset, so nothing overlaps.
